Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the start of West Indies' reply. The two umpires make their way out to the middle, followed by the two openers, Alick Athanaze and Brandon King. Added to the squad after the first ODI, Nasum Ahmed will open the attack for Bangladesh. Nasum to Alick with a slip in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Mehidy Hasan Miraz, at the toss, had mentioned that 230-240 could be a very good total on this track. While Bangladesh have fallen slightly short of that mark, 213 is still a competitive total, and the Bangladeshi spinners will be a handful in these spin-friendly conditions. West Indies will need someone like Roston Chase or Shai Hope to take responsibility and anchor the chase. It promises to be an interesting second half of the game. Stay tuned!

Most of the dismissals came as a result of batters trying to break free and go for the big shots, a reflection of how well the West Indies spinners kept them in check. In fact, all 50 overs were bowled by spin, yes, you read that right, the first time in ODI cricket history that a team has bowled 50 overs of spin. Mehidy Hasan Miraz tried to take charge after Sarkar's departure, but none of the knocks were as precious as Rishad Hossain’s. On a track where most batters batted at a strike rate under 100, Hossain blasted at 278.57, scoring a 14-ball 39 that propelled his side past 200.

Tremendous finish from Bangladesh! 34 runs came off the last two overs, and that has lifted them to 213. A tale of batters getting starts but none going on to make it big. There may not be any fifties on the card, yet Bangladesh have managed to post a competitive total. Soumya Sarkar stood out among the top five, holding one end firm as wickets kept tumbling around him.

A couple of runs to end the innings! Akeal Hosein tosses it up, full and on off, Rishad Hossain looks to go big again but gets a top edge. Keacy Carty from extra covers runs towards the mid off region and long off also runs forward, but in the end, both leave it for each other. Carty puts in a dive but does not get a hand to it. Two taken. Bangladesh finish on 213/7!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! First, Tawhid Hridoy and now Najmul Hossain Shanto both got starts but couldn’t convert. On a wicket like this, once you are set, it’s imperative to make it count. The surface has behaved as expected. While the sharp turn hasn’t been consistent, there’s been enough grip and turn to keep the batters on their toes. From Bangladesh’s perspective, despite the setbacks, it’s important to bat positively because on a pitch like this, there’s always that one delivery with your name on it. With both frontline pacers left out for this game, it’s been all spin from West Indies so far, and Shai Hope has cleverly kept the field up, tempting the hosts into taking risks. Mahidul Islam Ankon is the new man in for Bangladesh.

PITCH REPORT - Farveez Maharoof is near the surface and notes that there’s hardly a blade of grass, with this pitch looking even drier than the one used in the first game. Samuel Badree adds that it’s no surprise Bangladesh have added another spinner, while West Indies have opted to drop their two frontline pacers given the conditions. Shares that the surface has a mosaic pattern, the cracks have already started to open up, and spin is expected to play a pivotal role once again. He opines that playing late will be key on this surface and using the depth of the crease will be crucial, something Tawhid Hridoy did particularly well in the previous game, and something the West Indies batters will need to take note of.
Darren Sammy, the head coach of the West Indies, presents a maiden ODI cap to Ackeem Auguste. The left-handed batter becomes the 228th male player to represent the West Indies in ODIs.

The captain of West Indies, Shai Hope shares that they have had positive discussions on how to tackle spin in the middle phase of the game. Adds that they are looking forward to today's challenge. Believes that the surface is spin friendly but there will be help for the pacers if they can bowl in the right areas. Feels that if you are disciplined with your lines and lengths, it is difficult to score for batters on such tracks. Informs that they have made two changes with Akeal Hosein and Ackeem Auguste coming into the side with Auguste making his ODI debut.

The captain of Bangladesh, Mehidy Hasan Miraz believes that 230-240 is a very good total on this surface and they could have scored 30 runs more in the last game had they batted the entire 50 overs. Praises Mahidul Islam Ankon's knock and says they didn't expect a debutant to play such fearless cricket. Mentions that the partnership between Hridoy and Ankon was the turning point after they lost early wickets. Informs they have made one change as Nasum Ahmed comes in for Taskin Ahmed.

TOSS - Bangladesh have won the toss and they will BAT first.

The last three ODI series between these two sides in Bangladesh have all gone in favour of the hosts. Bangladesh will be eager to extend that streak and, in doing so, end their own drought, having lost each of their last four ODI series. Do the West Indies have it in them to mount a strong response, or will Bangladesh come out on top once again and put the series to bed? Stick around for the toss and team news.

On the other hand, the West Indies bowlers did a commendable job in restricting Bangladesh to a manageable total, but the batting unit failed to capitalise on a promising start. For the visitors to draw level in the series, experienced players like Roston Chase and captain Shai Hope will need to step up in what is expected to be another stern test against spin. Gudakesh Motie, surprisingly, went wicketless in the series opener, and the tourists will be counting on him to make a greater impact this time around.

On a dark surface, Bangladesh’s spinners ruled the roost, with Rishad Hossain’s six-wicket haul sealing the deal in the first ODI. The inclusion of Nasum Ahmed further strengthens their spin department, and the hosts will once again rely heavily on their spin attack to make the most of conditions. Despite emerging victorious in the opener, their struggles with the bat continued. ... MATCH DAY ...

The ODI series between Bangladesh and the West Indies moves to its second chapter in Mirpur. Bangladesh landed the first blow in the series and will now aim to seal it with another win, while West Indies will be eager to bounce back and take the contest to a decider. The visitors’ bowlers did their job well, bowling the hosts out for 207, but their batting faltered after a steady 51-run opening stand. Rishad Hossain made full use of the spin-friendly conditions, claiming six wickets to spin Bangladesh to victory. With similar conditions anticipated, the Windies will need greater contributions from Brandon King, Roston Chase, Sherfane Rutherford, and skipper Shai Hope to steady their batting effort. On the bowling front, much will depend on the spin trio of Khary Pierre, Chase, and Gudakesh Motie, while Jayden Seales and Romario Shepherd will look to set the tone with the new ball. On the other hand, the Bangla Tigers left much to be desired with the bat, with their woes from the Afghanistan series continuing. Najmul Hossain Shanto, Tawhid Hridoy, Saif Hassan, and Soumya Sarkar will be crucial as the Asian side looks to deliver a more solid batting display than in their recent outings. Considering that the entire ODI series is being played in Mirpur, the hosts have strengthened their spin attack with the addition of left-arm spinner Nasum Ahmed. Whether he features in the second ODI remains to be seen, but the home side will be banking on Rishad Hossain and captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz to do the job in the spin department. Bangladesh have lost their last four ODI series but now have an opportunity to spark a revival of their 50-over campaign with a win in the second ODI. West Indies, on the other hand, will be desperate to respond and keep the series alive. Who will seize the moment in Mirpur?
